text:
ops-bot: 🔔 Incident alert: p99 latency spike detected on cont-batch path in us-west-2. Streaming requests showing stalls and increased timeouts. Auto-pager triggered. Investigate please.

maria_g: oncall here, looking. seeing p95 ~ 420ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 3.2s -> 12s on streaming RPCs to model-redwood-enc-2. timeline: spike started ~ 5876543000.

ashok: confirmed. telemetry shows cont-batcher queue depth jump and many mixed-seqlen batches with high padding. KV cache churn increased too. likely packing amplification.

sam_k: any recent deploys to batching scheduler? I pushed a scheduling tweak yesterday that increased pack window to 8ms in us-west-2.

maria_g: yep that matches. I'm rolling metrics for last deploy and correlating.

infra-bot: deploy event detected: scheduler-service v2.9.1 -> v2.10.0 at 5876529000 (user: sam_k). Changed parameter: pack_window_ms: 4 -> 8.

taylor: paging note: two customers reported degraded streaming throughput (retries observed). no broad 5xx spikes yet but tail latency causing client timeouts.

ashok: digging into traces. lots of streaming requests are getting batched with long-tail small requests. scheduler is favoring throughput and ends up holding streaming packets to fill batches -> increased tail.

maria_g: mitigation options: 1) revert pack_window to 4ms (quick rollback of scheduler flag) 2) enable preemptive streaming priority (schedule streaming ahead of long-running jobs) 3) reduce max_batch_size for cont-batch on streaming route 4) route streaming to dedicated pool (if capacity)

sam_k: I can roll back pack_window to 4ms quickly. patch and rollout in 2-3 mins? also add temporary override: streaming_priority=true for us-west-2.

maria_g: please do rollout as step 1. while that's happening, I'll open a live-tail of cont-batcher logs and start counting evicted KV entries and padding ratio.

ashok: note: padding amplification metric at 5876543100 = 2.6x; KV-ejection spikes at same time. probably mixed-seqlen requests (many short prompts) are causing large batches to pad.

sam_k: rolling back pack_window now. command: `kubectl set env deployment/scheduler pack_window_ms=4 -n infra` -> launching canary in us-west-2.

infra-bot: rollout started: scheduler-service/us-west-2 canary pod(s) updated (by sam_k). Watch: https://infra.redwood/rollouts/5876543211

maria_g: can we also set `streaming_route.max_batch_tokens=1024` from 2048 to lower padding? that'll reduce batch wait for streaming.

ashok: yep that is lower-risk. I'll prepare the config patch and apply to routing config (hot reload supported).

sam_k: can confirm canary pod passed health checks. rolling to 30% -> 100% over next 2m.

taylor: customer impact update: Customer A (streaming video captions) seeing retries down from 18% -> 6% just after canary started.

maria_g: good signal. Request: enable `preempt_streaming=true` for cont-batch scheduler as temporary for next 30m to reclaim SLO.

ashok: preempt flag requires scheduler restart? it's a dynamic config via /admin API. I'll flip it.

ashok: flipping `preempt_streaming=true` now. curl -XPOST 'https://scheduler.us-west-2/admin/config' -d '{"preempt_streaming":true}'

infra-bot: admin config change recorded by ashok at 5876543385: preempt_streaming=true

maria_g: latency graphs: p99 trending down from 12s -> 2.6s in 60s. p95 back to ~350ms. This looks like rollback + preempt did the trick. Keep an eye for oscillation.

sam_k: applied `streaming_route.max_batch_tokens=1024` at 5876543440. also added a short-term pack cap: `max_pack_size_tokens=4096`.

taylor: noting: some longer-generation customers might see slightly reduced throughput but lower tail. flagged to support.

maria_g: can someone add a temporary routing policy to route high-latency customers to dedicated low-latency pool if they opt-in? we can avoid broad perf impact.

ashok: added route rule: header X-LLM-Prefer: lowlatency -> dedicated-pool-usw2. live since 5876543550.

sam_k: slow-deploy rollback observed -> all scheduler pods at 4ms pack window now. no config drift.

maria_g: good. next steps: 1) continue monitoring for 15m 2) capture trace for a sampling of affected requests 3) start on-call handoff notes for next shift 4) prepare postmortem if SLO breach confirmed

taylor: I'll notify support and open ticket for Customer A with remediation notes and ETA.

ashok: saved traces to /traces/5876543211/spike-sample-1 and uploaded heap of KV-snapshots. also created a short eval showing mixed-seqlen distribution: 78% < 64 tokens, 12% > 1024 tokens.

maria_g: action items (quick):
- sam_k: revert pack_window (done) + confirm rollout (done)
- ashok: preempt_streaming flip + trace dumps (done)
- taylor: customer comms + support ticket (in progress)
- infra-bot: keep collecting padding_ratio, p95/p99, queue_depth

sam_k: putting a short note in changelog: revert of pack_window after observed tail impact. will draft an RFC on pack-window tradeoffs.

infra-bot: metric alert cleared at 5876543690: cont-batch p99 > 5s resolved.

maria_g: handing off to next oncall @ashok for further follow-up and postmortem. I'm off in ~10m.

ashok: taking over. I'll run a deeper sim for mixed-seqlen behavior and propose a scheduler change that weights streaming requests by latency-sensitivity not just token count.

taylor: thx all. I'll ping customers with update. :thumbsup:

maria_g: final: please record timestamps and config states in the incident tracker. I'll start the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/5876543211

ops-bot: Incident acknowledged and assigned: incident-5876543211. Severity: sev2 (SLO impact but mitigated). Next update due in 30m.

ashok: noted. oncall handoff complete. follow-up owners: ashok (root cause analysis), sam_k (scheduler RFC), taylor (customer comms). Closing slack thread when postmortem link is live.
